questions.prompt: How fast can a cheetah sprint at full tilt, in km/h?
questions.reveal: A cheetah hits 100 km/h in about three seconds, but the whole chase is usually over in under 30 seconds before it overheats.

questions.prompt: Fastest bird ever clocked in a dive: what speed did a peregrine falcon hit, in km/h?
questions.reveal: Peregrines have baffles in their nostrils that slow the incoming air, so their lungs don't burst at that speed.

questions.prompt: Top speed commonly credited to a sailfish, the ocean's speed demon, in km/h?
questions.reveal: Sailfish flash electric blue stripes when hunting, a mood change produced by pigment cells firing in milliseconds.

questions.prompt: Top running speed of an ostrich, the fastest two-legged animal on land, in km/h?
questions.reveal: An ostrich has just two toes per foot, and one of them carries almost all the weight, like a sprinter's spike.

questions.prompt: How fast can a black mamba slither across open ground, in km/h?
questions.reveal: That makes it the fastest snake on Earth, though it would still lose a footrace to a jogging human.

questions.prompt: A common garden snail cruises at roughly what speed, in centimeters per second?
questions.reveal: Snails glide on a ribbon of mucus they secrete as they go, which lets them cross a razor blade unharmed.

questions.prompt: A ruby-throated hummingbird beats its wings how many times per second in normal flight?
questions.reveal: Their wings trace a figure eight, which is why they are the only birds that can fly properly backwards.

questions.prompt: During a deep dive, a blue whale's heart can slow to how few beats per minute?
questions.reveal: At the surface it rockets back up to about 37 beats a minute, near the theoretical maximum for a heart that size.

questions.prompt: A bloodhound's nose packs roughly how many scent receptors?
questions.reveal: A bloodhound's trail evidence has been accepted in court, and the loose facial skin helps waft scent up toward the nose.

questions.prompt: How long was the longest blue whale ever reliably measured, in meters?
questions.reveal: No dinosaur came close: the blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived on Earth.

questions.prompt: The colossal squid has the animal kingdom's biggest eye. How wide is it, in cm?
questions.reveal: That is roughly a dinner plate, built to catch the faint glow of prey a kilometer down in the dark.

questions.prompt: The bee hummingbird, the world's smallest bird, tips the scales at how many grams?
questions.reveal: It weighs less than a Canadian penny, and its nest is about the size of a thimble.

questions.prompt: An ostrich egg, the largest egg laid by any living animal, weighs about how many kg?
questions.reveal: The shell is so thick it takes about 90 minutes to hard-boil, and an adult human can stand on an intact one.

questions.prompt: The heaviest insect ever recorded, a giant weta, weighed how many grams?
questions.reveal: That is heavier than a sparrow. New Zealand's wetas grew large in the absence of land mammals to eat them.

questions.prompt: A sperm whale's brain, the largest on Earth, weighs about how many kg?
questions.reveal: About five times a human brain, and it sits behind a head full of spermaceti oil used for echolocation.

questions.prompt: How long is a giraffe's tongue, in centimeters?
questions.reveal: It is a dark purple-black, likely a sunscreen for an organ that spends all day out in the African sun.

questions.prompt: A newborn giant panda cub weighs about how many grams?
questions.reveal: That is roughly 1/900th of its mother, and the cub is born pink, blind and nearly hairless.

questions.prompt: A newborn red kangaroo joey weighs roughly how many grams?
questions.reveal: Blind and jellybean-sized, it crawls unaided through its mother's fur to the pouch, a journey of about three minutes.

questions.prompt: The longest snake ever recorded, a reticulated python, measured how many meters?
questions.reveal: Reticulated pythons can unhinge their jaws via a stretchy ligament, swallowing prey wider than their own head.

questions.prompt: A saltwater crocodile's bite has been measured at roughly how many newtons of force?
questions.reveal: The muscles that open those jaws are so weak that a few loops of tape can hold a croc's mouth shut.

questions.prompt: An elephant's trunk contains roughly how many muscles?
questions.reveal: There is not a single bone in there, yet it can uproot a tree or pick up one tortilla chip without breaking it.

questions.prompt: A North American porcupine carries about how many quills?
questions.reveal: Porcupines cannot shoot their quills; the barbed tips simply detach on contact and work deeper with every muscle twitch.

questions.prompt: Deepest dive by any bird: how far down did an emperor penguin go, in meters?
questions.reveal: Emperors can stay under for more than 20 minutes, hardening their bones so they don't collapse under pressure.

questions.prompt: The record dive by a Cuvier's beaked whale reached what depth, in meters?
questions.reveal: The same species holds the mammal breath-hold record: one whale stayed under for 3 hours and 42 minutes.

questions.prompt: How deep is Challenger Deep, the lowest known point in the ocean, in meters?
questions.reveal: Drop Mount Everest in and its summit would still be more than 2 km underwater.

questions.prompt: How tall is Mount Everest above sea level, per the 2020 China-Nepal survey, in meters?
questions.reveal: The summit rock is marine limestone: it was once seafloor, shoved skyward by India crashing into Asia.

questions.prompt: Hyperion, the world's tallest known tree, stands how many meters tall?
questions.reveal: Its exact location in Redwood National Park is a secret, and visiting it now carries a fine.

questions.prompt: Methuselah, a Great Basin bristlecone pine, is roughly how many years old?
questions.reveal: It was already a sapling when the Great Pyramid was being built, and it still produces viable seeds.

questions.prompt: The fastest-growing bamboo can shoot up how many centimeters in a single day?
questions.reveal: That is roughly 4 cm an hour, fast enough that a patient observer can actually watch it happen. Individual stalks have been clocked past 120 cm.

questions.prompt: The Arctic tern's yearly round-trip migration covers roughly how many km?
questions.reveal: Chasing two summers a year, an Arctic tern sees more daylight in its life than any other animal.

questions.prompt: A monarch butterfly's one-way migration to central Mexico can span how many km?
questions.reveal: No single butterfly makes the round trip; it takes three or four generations to complete the circuit.

questions.prompt: A bar-tailed godwit flew nonstop from Alaska to Tasmania in 2022. How many km was it?
questions.reveal: It flew for 11 days without landing, eating or drinking, having shrunk its own digestive organs to save weight.

questions.prompt: How many months does an African elephant stay pregnant?
questions.reveal: The longest gestation of any land mammal, and the calf arrives already weighing around 120 kg.

questions.prompt: The Virginia opossum has one of the shortest mammal pregnancies: how many days?
questions.reveal: The bee-sized newborns finish developing in the pouch, where a whole litter can fit in a tablespoon.

questions.prompt: The longest-cycle periodical cicada broods stay underground for how many years?
questions.reveal: Prime-numbered cycles of 13 and 17 years make it nearly impossible for predators to sync their own boom years.

questions.prompt: The shortest-lived adult mayfly, female Dolania americana, survives about how many minutes?
questions.reveal: She emerges, mates, drops her eggs and dies before breakfast, having spent nearly two years as a larva.

questions.prompt: At peak season, a queen honeybee can lay how many eggs in a single day?
questions.reveal: That is more than her own body weight in eggs daily, laid one per cell at roughly one every 20 seconds.

questions.prompt: How many years can a Greenland shark, the longest-lived vertebrate, live?
questions.reveal: They don't reach sexual maturity until about age 150, and many carry a parasite dangling from each eye.

questions.prompt: 'Ming' the ocean quahog clam was how many years old when scientists finally aged it?
questions.reveal: Researchers accidentally killed it while prying it open, then had to recount the rings to correct an earlier estimate.

questions.prompt: Creme Puff, the oldest cat ever verified, lived how many years?
questions.reveal: Her Texas owner reportedly fed her bacon, eggs, broccoli and a splash of coffee with cream.

questions.prompt: A koala spends how many hours of each day asleep?
questions.reveal: Eucalyptus leaves are so low in energy and so full of toxins that sleeping is basically a digestion strategy.

questions.prompt: How many vertebrae are in a giraffe's very long neck?
questions.reveal: The same number as a human, a mouse and a whale: each giraffe vertebra is just up to 25 cm long.

questions.prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.reveal: Two pump blood through the gills and one serves the body, and that one stops beating when the octopus swims.

questions.prompt: How many eyes does a honeybee have, counting the simple ones on top of its head?
questions.reveal: Two big compound eyes plus three tiny ocelli that track sunlight and keep the bee level in flight.

questions.prompt: How many chambers does a cow's stomach have?
questions.reveal: The rumen alone can hold around 150 liters, a fermentation vat run entirely by microbes.

questions.prompt: The leggiest animal ever found, the millipede Eumillipes persephone, had how many legs?
questions.reveal: It was discovered 60 meters down a mining borehole in Western Australia, blind and thread-thin.

questions.prompt: How many teeth does an adult dog have?
questions.reveal: Puppies get 28 baby teeth and swap the lot out by about six months, usually swallowing them unnoticed.

questions.prompt: A garden snail's rasping tongue carries roughly how many microscopic teeth?
questions.reveal: The radula works like a chainsaw belt, and limpet versions of it are made of the strongest known biological material.

questions.prompt: How many chromosomes does a domestic dog have?
questions.reveal: That is 39 pairs against a human's 23, which is one reason dog genetics gets messy fast.

questions.prompt: Roughly how many beetle species have scientists formally described?
questions.reveal: About one in four known animal species is a beetle, which prompted a famous quip about the Creator's fondness for them.

questions.prompt: Roughly how many living bird species do ornithologists currently recognize?
questions.reveal: The count keeps creeping up, not from new discoveries but from DNA splitting old species into several.

questions.prompt: A 2022 study estimated how many individual ants are alive on Earth?
questions.reveal: Their combined dry weight outweighs all wild birds and mammals put together.

questions.prompt: The longest beaver dam on record, spotted from space in Canada, stretches how many meters?
questions.source: Wood Buffalo National Park, Parks Canada
questions.reveal: It is visible in satellite imagery and was probably started in the 1970s by generations of the same family.

questions.prompt: The heaviest bird nest ever recorded, built by bald eagles, weighed about how many kg?
questions.reveal: Eagles reuse and enlarge nests for decades; this Florida one was nearly 3 m wide and 6 m deep.

questions.prompt: An ocean sunfish can carry how many eggs at once, the most of any known vertebrate?
questions.reveal: A sunfish larva is about 2.5 mm long and grows up to 60 million times heavier, the biggest size jump in vertebrates.

Guinness 389 km/h (242 mph) confirmed; bounds adequate.
110 km/h disputed scientifically, but prompt hedges with 'commonly credited'.
70 km/h standard ostrich figure; bounds fine.
Guinness says 16-19 km/h; reveal's 'loses to a jogger' claim is false.
1.3 cm/s equals the standard 0.048 km/h figure.
Cornell states 53 wingbeats per second; bounds fine.
Stanford 2019: minimum 2 bpm, 37 bpm at surface.
300 million receptors is the universally cited bloodhound figure.
Longest reliably measured 33.58 m; 33 within tolerance.
Te Papa measured about 27 cm; largest known animal eye.
Bee hummingbird ~1.6-2 g; bounds have adequate margin.
Ostrich eggs average ~1.4 kg; bounds acceptable.
Sperm whale brain ~7.8 kg, largest known; bounds fine.
Giraffe tongue 45-50 cm; answer within range.
Red kangaroo neonate about 0.8-1 g; correct.

300 million eggs, most fecund vertebrate; confirmed.

questions.prompt: Light in a vacuum covers how many kilometres in a single second?
questions.reveal: Since 1983 the metre has been defined by this speed, so light's speed can never be measured wrong again.

questions.prompt: How far is the Moon from Earth on average, centre to centre, in km?
questions.reveal: Every other planet in the solar system could be lined up side by side in the gap between Earth and the Moon.

questions.prompt: How many km from Earth to the Sun on average, i.e. one astronomical unit?
questions.reveal: The AU is now fixed by definition at exactly 149,597,870,700 metres, so nobody has to remeasure it.

questions.prompt: How wide is the Sun across its equator, in km?
questions.reveal: Line up 109 Earths edge to edge and you would just about span the face of the Sun.

questions.prompt: Jupiter is the solar system's giant. How wide is it at the equator, in km?
questions.reveal: Jupiter spins once in under 10 hours, which bulges it out about 9,000 km wider at the equator than pole to pole.

questions.prompt: How many km across is Earth, measured at the equator?
questions.reveal: Earth is 43 km fatter through the equator than through the poles, so it is a very slightly squashed ball.

questions.prompt: How many km across is the Moon?
questions.reveal: That is just over a quarter of Earth's width, the largest moon-to-planet ratio anywhere in the solar system.

questions.prompt: A year on Mercury: how many Earth days does one orbit of the Sun take?
questions.reveal: One Mercury day-night cycle lasts 176 Earth days, which is two full Mercury years of sunlight and dark.

questions.prompt: How many Earth years does Neptune need to orbit the Sun once?
questions.reveal: Discovered in 1846, Neptune only completed its first full orbit since discovery in 2011.

questions.prompt: Venus spins painfully slowly. How many Earth days does one Venus rotation take?
questions.reveal: Venus takes longer to spin once than to orbit the Sun in 225 days, and it spins backwards while doing it.

questions.prompt: A Martian sol runs longer than an Earth day. By how many minutes?
questions.reveal: Rover teams live on Mars time, sliding their whole working day about 40 minutes later every single day.

questions.prompt: How many light-years away is Proxima Centauri, the nearest star to our Sun?
questions.reveal: Voyager 1, our fastest departing probe, would need roughly 70,000 years to cover that distance.

questions.prompt: One light-year equals how many trillion km?
questions.reveal: Despite the name, a light-year measures distance, not time, which trips up screenwriters constantly.

questions.prompt: Roughly how many light-years across is the disc of the Milky Way?
questions.reveal: Light leaving one rim of the galaxy today will still be crossing it when human civilisation is ancient history.

questions.prompt: How old is the universe, in billions of years?
questions.reveal: The figure comes from the cosmic microwave background, the faint afterglow of light released 380,000 years in.

questions.prompt: How old is planet Earth, in billions of years?
questions.reveal: The age comes from lead isotopes in meteorites, because Earth's own original crust was long ago recycled away.

questions.prompt: How many minutes does sunlight take to travel from the Sun to Earth?
questions.source: derived from the speed of light and 1 AU
questions.reveal: If the Sun switched off, we would carry on sunbathing for over eight minutes before anyone noticed.

questions.prompt: How many Earths would fit inside the Sun, by volume?
questions.reveal: By mass the Sun is even more dominant: it holds 99.86% of everything in the solar system.

questions.prompt: How fast does the International Space Station orbit Earth, in km/h?
questions.reveal: At that pace the crew laps the planet every 90 minutes and sees 16 sunrises a day.

questions.prompt: How fast must a rocket travel to escape Earth's gravity, in km/s?
questions.reveal: That is about 40,300 km/h. On the Moon a gentle 2.4 km/s would be enough to leave for good.

questions.prompt: How hot is the visible surface of the Sun, the photosphere, in kelvin?
questions.reveal: Sunspots look black only by contrast. At around 3,800 K they would still outshine any furnace on Earth.

questions.prompt: How hot is the Sun's core, in millions of kelvin?
questions.reveal: At that heat and pressure the core fuses roughly 600 million tonnes of hydrogen every second.

questions.prompt: Venus is the hottest planet. What is its average surface temperature in Celsius?
questions.reveal: Hot enough to melt lead, and barely changing between day and night thanks to a runaway CO2 greenhouse.

questions.prompt: Standing on Jupiter's cloud tops, what would surface gravity be in m/s squared?
questions.reveal: You would weigh about two and a half times more. Jupiter's sheer size softens what its huge mass would otherwise do.

questions.prompt: How many years does Halley's Comet take to swing back past Earth?
questions.reveal: Last seen in 1986 and due back in 2061, most people get at most one viewing in a lifetime.

questions.prompt: How many kg of Moon rock and soil did the six Apollo landings bring home in total?
questions.reveal: Some samples are still sealed and deliberately unopened, waiting for instruments nobody has invented yet.

questions.prompt: As of 2024, how many people have walked on the surface of the Moon?
questions.reveal: All twelve walked between 1969 and 1972, and every one of them flew on an Apollo mission.

questions.prompt: Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest volcano known. How many km does it rise?
questions.reveal: It is roughly 600 km wide, so standing on it the slope would vanish over the horizon before the summit appeared.

questions.prompt: At what temperature in Celsius does liquid nitrogen boil at sea level?
questions.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics
questions.reveal: Splash it on the floor and it skitters, because each droplet rides on a cushion of its own vapour.

questions.prompt: Helium boils at the lowest temperature of any element. What is it, in kelvin?
questions.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics
questions.reveal: Chill it below 2.17 K and it becomes a superfluid that climbs the walls of its container and escapes.

questions.prompt: Absolute zero sits at what temperature in Celsius?
questions.reveal: It is unreachable in principle. Labs have hit billionths of a degree above it, but never zero itself.

questions.prompt: Tungsten has the highest melting point of any metal. What is it, in Celsius?
questions.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics
questions.reveal: That stubbornness is why tungsten filaments glowed white-hot inside light bulbs for a century without melting.

questions.prompt: At what temperature in Celsius does iron melt?
questions.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics
questions.reveal: Earth's inner core is far hotter than this and still solid, because crushing pressure beats heat.

questions.prompt: At what temperature in Celsius does pure gold melt?
questions.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics
questions.reveal: Gold is so unreactive that almost every gram ever melted down still exists somewhere on Earth today.

questions.prompt: Mercury is liquid at room temperature. At what Celsius does it finally freeze?
questions.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics
questions.reveal: Frozen mercury turns into a soft, dull metal you could dent with a fingernail.

questions.prompt: Dry ice skips being liquid. At what Celsius does solid CO2 turn straight to gas?
questions.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics
questions.reveal: That solid-to-gas leap is called sublimation, and it is exactly why dry ice never leaves a puddle.

questions.prompt: Osmium is the densest natural element. What is its density in kg per cubic metre?
questions.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics
questions.reveal: A one-litre bottle of osmium weighs about 22.6 kg, roughly a full airline carry-on bag.

questions.prompt: How many protons are packed into a single atom of gold?
questions.reveal: Take one proton away and you get platinum. The alchemists were only ever one particle out.

questions.prompt: As of 2024, how many chemical elements appear on the periodic table?
questions.reveal: Everything past uranium is synthetic, and element 118, oganesson, survives for less than a millisecond.

questions.prompt: How many chemical elements are named after the tiny Swedish village of Ytterby?
questions.reveal: Yttrium, ytterbium, terbium and erbium all came out of one small quarry. No other place on Earth comes close.

questions.prompt: How fast does sound travel through dry air at 20 Celsius, in m/s?
questions.reveal: Every extra degree of warmth adds about 0.6 m/s, so sound genuinely travels quicker on a hot afternoon.

questions.prompt: Sound moving through fresh water at 20 Celsius travels how many m/s?
questions.reveal: Water carries sound over four times faster than air, which is how whale song crosses entire ocean basins.

questions.prompt: How many times could a light beam lap Earth's equator in one second?
questions.source: derived from speed of light and Earth's circumference
questions.reveal: Even at that pace, a call bounced off a distant satellite still lands with a delay you can hear.

questions.prompt: What percentage of Earth's dry atmosphere is nitrogen, by volume?
questions.reveal: Oxygen is only 21%, so the gas we actually depend on is very much the sidekick in every breath.

questions.prompt: How many bones are there in a typical adult human skeleton?
questions.reveal: More than half of them are in your hands and feet: 106 bones sit below the wrists and ankles.

questions.prompt: How many chromosomes are in a typical human body cell?
questions.reveal: That is 23 pairs. A potato has 48, so chromosome count says nothing at all about sophistication.

questions.prompt: What percentage of the human body's mass is made up of oxygen atoms?
questions.reveal: Almost all of it is locked inside water. Carbon comes a distant second at around 18%.

questions.prompt: Roughly how many times does an average adult human heart beat in a single day?
questions.reveal: That works out to roughly 2.5 billion beats across a lifetime, with no maintenance breaks allowed.

questions.prompt: How many litres of blood does a resting adult heart pump every minute?
questions.reveal: Your whole blood supply is about 5 litres, so the entire lot completes a lap roughly every minute.

questions.prompt: Laid end to end, how many km of blood vessels are in an adult human body?
questions.reveal: That is two and a half times around the equator, and most of it is capillaries thinner than a hair.

questions.prompt: How many days does a human red blood cell survive before it is recycled?
questions.reveal: Your spleen retires about two million of them every second while your marrow builds replacements just as fast.

questions.prompt: Unwound and stretched out, the DNA in one human cell measures how many metres?
questions.reveal: Add up every cell in your body and that thread would reach the Sun and back hundreds of times over.

questions.prompt: How many billion base pairs make up one set of the human genome?
questions.reveal: Written out in tiny type it would fill about a million pages, and 99.9% of it matches the person next to you.

questions.prompt: How many billion neurons are in the average adult human brain?
questions.source: Azevedo et al. neuron counting study
questions.reveal: The old textbook figure of 100 billion was a guess. Researchers finally counted by dissolving brains into a soup.

questions.prompt: What is the top speed of a nerve signal in the human body, in m/s?
questions.reveal: That is about 430 km/h on fat myelinated motor nerves, while dull pain signals crawl at under 1 m/s.

questions.prompt: One small step: in what year did Apollo 11 first land humans on the Moon?
questions.reveal: Neil Armstrong's boot prints are still up there — the Moon has no wind to blow them away.

questions.prompt: The 'unsinkable' Titanic struck an iceberg and sank in what year?
questions.reveal: The band famously kept playing as the ship went down; the wreck itself wasn't found until 1985.

questions.prompt: In what year was the US Declaration of Independence adopted in Philadelphia?
questions.reveal: Most delegates actually signed on August 2 — weeks after the famous July 4 adoption.

questions.prompt: In what year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.reveal: A botched press-conference answer — 'immediately, without delay' — opened the border that very night.

questions.prompt: In what year did Columbus first reach the Americas?
questions.reveal: Columbus made four voyages and went to his grave insisting he had reached Asia.

questions.prompt: In what year did World War I begin?
questions.reveal: Sparked by an assassination in Sarajevo, the war ultimately toppled four empires.

questions.prompt: The very first iPhone went on sale in what year?
questions.reveal: Steve Jobs pitched it as three devices in one: an iPod, a phone, and an 'internet communicator'.

questions.prompt: The Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flight at Kitty Hawk in what year?
questions.reveal: That first flight lasted 12 seconds — shorter than a modern airliner's wingspan is long.

questions.prompt: Japan attacked Pearl Harbor in what year?
questions.reveal: The attack lasted about 90 minutes and pulled the United States into World War II the next day.

questions.prompt: President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas in what year?
questions.reveal: The Zapruder home movie of the motorcade became one of the most scrutinized films in history.

questions.prompt: The original Star Wars film first hit theaters in what year?
questions.reveal: It opened in just 32 US theaters — studio executives were bracing for a flop.

questions.prompt: Larry Page and Sergey Brin founded Google in what year?
questions.reveal: The pair once tried to sell their search engine for under a million dollars — and were turned down.

questions.prompt: Wikipedia went live in what year?
questions.reveal: It now spans tens of millions of articles in over 300 languages — all volunteer-written.

questions.prompt: Disneyland opened its gates in Anaheim, California in what year?
questions.reveal: Opening day was nicknamed 'Black Sunday' — a heat wave melted the freshly laid asphalt.

questions.prompt: The first Harry Potter book was published in the UK in what year?
questions.reveal: The first print run was just 500 copies — and about 300 of those went to libraries.

questions.prompt: The Chernobyl nuclear disaster happened in what year?
questions.reveal: The city of Pripyat was evacuated in a single afternoon — 36 hours after the explosion.

questions.prompt: The Eiffel Tower was completed in Paris in what year?
questions.reveal: It was meant to be torn down after 20 years — its usefulness as a radio antenna saved it.

questions.prompt: Parisians stormed the Bastille, igniting the French Revolution, in what year?

questions.prompt: New Zealand became the first country to give women the national vote in what year?

questions.prompt: The Montgolfier brothers' balloon carried the first humans into the sky in what year?

questions.prompt: Karl von Drais rode the very first bicycle — no pedals yet — in what year?

questions.prompt: Harvard, the oldest university in the United States, was founded in what year?

questions.prompt: Ray Tomlinson sent the first ever email between computers in what year?

questions.prompt: The Mona Lisa was stolen from the Louvre in what year?

questions.prompt: The WHO officially declared smallpox eradicated worldwide in what year?

questions.prompt: Chinese farmers digging a well discovered the Terracotta Army in what year?

questions.prompt: Concorde carried its first paying supersonic passengers in what year?

questions.prompt: John Logie Baird first demonstrated true television to a live audience in what year?

questions.prompt: Euro banknotes and coins first jingled in European pockets in what year?

questions.prompt: The oldest surviving photograph was taken by Nicéphore Niépce in what year?

questions.prompt: The volcano Krakatoa blew itself apart in a colossal eruption in what year?

questions.prompt: James Naismith invented basketball in a Massachusetts gym in what year?

questions.prompt: The Beatles made their famous US debut on The Ed Sullivan Show in what year?

questions.prompt: Bitcoin's very first block — the genesis block — was mined in what year?

questions.prompt: King John sealed the Magna Carta at Runnymede in what year?

questions.prompt: William the Conqueror won the Battle of Hastings in what year?

questions.prompt: Charlemagne was crowned emperor by the Pope on Christmas Day of what year?

questions.prompt: Emperor Hadrian began building his famous wall across Britain in what year AD?

questions.prompt: Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii in what year AD?

questions.prompt: Constantinople fell to the Ottoman Empire in what year?

questions.prompt: Gutenberg finished printing his famous Bible — Europe's first major printed book — in what year?

questions.prompt: Plague ships brought the Black Death to Sicily — its arrival in Europe — in what year?

questions.prompt: Temujin was proclaimed Genghis Khan, ruler of all Mongols, in what year?

questions.prompt: England's navy — with help from storms — defeated the Spanish Armada in what year?

questions.prompt: The Mayflower carried the Pilgrims across the Atlantic in what year?
questions.reveal: Its 102 passengers shared a living space about the size of a tennis court for 66 days.

questions.prompt: William Shakespeare died in Stratford-upon-Avon in what year?

questions.prompt: Galileo first pointed a telescope at the night sky in what year?

questions.prompt: Isaac Newton published the Principia, laying out his laws of motion, in what year?

questions.prompt: The Great Fire of London torched the city in what year?

questions.prompt: French soldiers in Egypt unearthed the Rosetta Stone in what year?

questions.prompt: Edward Jenner performed the first smallpox vaccination in what year?

questions.prompt: Ether was first publicly demonstrated as surgical anesthesia in Boston in what year?

questions.prompt: Height of Mount Everest above sea level, in metres?

questions.prompt: Commonly cited length of the Nile, the classic answer to 'world's longest river', in km?

questions.prompt: Total area of Russia, the world's biggest country, in millions of km²?

questions.prompt: How many billion humans were on Earth in 2024 (rounded)?
